pr_title: Make global scope enums accessible as types in GDScript
pr_body:
Add functions to CoreConstant so enums can be properly deduced. Also add the enums in release builds to make consistent with ClassDB enums and avoid differences in script compilation between debug and release.

Fix #72963
Fix #73046
Closes #72984 (superseded)

issue_context.title: `_parse_property` in `EditorInspectorPlugin` is asking for `::Type` instead of `int` in `type` parameter.
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0 rc1

### System information

Manjaro Linux using i3, Foward+

### Issue description

All of my `EditorInspectorPlugin`s are broken with the following error:
```
Line 34:The function signature doesn't match the parent. Parent signature is "_parse_property(Object, ::Type, String, int, String, int, bool) -> bool".
```

I tried to change it from `int` to `Type` like it shows in the documentation and it also doesn't work:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13070158/217805607-de1bc8f2-3c36-4f1c-9a6d-02b8e2bbee2d.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13070158/217805682-d43b3ccf-0fb7-4e7a-a9c3-92fd7e63be94.png)

And keeping it as an `int` just gives me the function signature mismatch error above.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a new `EditorInspectorPlugin` script and try to override the virtual method `_parse_property`

### Minimal reproduction project

See Steps to reproduce above.
comments: It looks like this was my fault (see https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/71479).

The type is actually `Variant.Type`, it's a nested type. The [online documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_editorinspectorplugin.html#class-editorinspectorplugin-method-parse-property) seems to be able to handle it properly, not sure why the editor documentation shows just `Type`.

However, it seems using `Variant.Type` is not usable as a type hint in GDScript, I get error `Variant doesn't contain nested types.`

I wonder why `int` is working for the other enums though.

The other enums have a data type of kind `GDScriptParser::DataType::BUILTIN` with builtin_type being `Variant::INT`, but `Variant.Type` has a datat type of kind `GDScriptParser::DataType::ENUM` which when turned into a string becomes `::Type` because the native class name is empty.

The `GDScriptAnalyzer::type_from_property` method creates the data types, and it seems it creates an enum datatype for `Variant.Type` because it checks if the name has a dot (`.`) in it. I wonder if we should add a special case for `Variant` enums.
